# Web Apps, SPAs (React/Next.js/Angular/Vue), SSR & Low-Code (`web-spa-nextjs-ssr`)

> **Group:** I. Web, Mobile & API Core
> **Product Archetypes:** SPA_Web_Frontend, Fullstack_Web_App, Ecommerce_Portal, LowCode_Admin_Portal
> **Trigger Signals:** react, nextjs, next, angular, vue, webpack, vite, sourcemap, ssr, nocobase, wordpress, php, spa, cors, csrf, xss

## [ BLOCK: nextjs-ssr-and-server-actions ]
### Next.js App/Pages Router, SSR Data Leaks & Server Actions
- Inspect `getServerSideProps`, React Server Components (RSC), and Server Actions (`'use server'`) for missing session/role checks.
- Verify whether full internal objects or admin routes (e.g., 900+ client routes in Next.js manifests) leak sensitive tenant/dealer logic or internal API base URLs.
- Check middleware bypass (`middleware.ts` matcher gaps, `x-middleware-subrequest`, path normalization).

## [ BLOCK: spa-sourcemap-and-bundle-secrets ]
### SPA Sourcemaps (.js.map), Environment Configs & Client-Side Auth Bypass
- Check build configs (`productionBrowserSourceMaps`, Vite/Webpack/Angular `sourceMap`) for `.js.map` exposure in prod/staging buckets.
- Inspect `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, `VITE_*`, `REACT_APP_*`, and `config.js` for leaked internal API gateways (`emp-non-prod-api`, OAuth client secrets, static HMAC keys).
- Enforce the H5 200-Falsehood rule: distinguish real asset/API responses from SPA `index.html` catch-all rewrites.

## [ BLOCK: dom-xss-postmessage-and-cors ]
### DOM XSS, postMessage Bridges, OAuth Redirects & Permissive CORS
- Trace `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` handlers without strict `event.origin` verification.
- Audit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reflection and staging/localhost origins (`http://localhost:3003`) enabled with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.
- Verify OAuth/OIDC `redirect_uri`, `state`, and PKCE validation against open-redirect token theft.

## [ BLOCK: general-injection-ssti-and-path-traversal ]
### Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), File Upload Path Traversal & DOM Sinks
- Trace dynamic template rendering (`Handlebars`, `EJS`, `Jinja2`, `Twig`, `Freemarker`) and SSR file-serving helpers (`path.join`, `sendFile`) for SSTI and `../` path traversal.
- Audit multipart uploads and static asset proxies for unvalidated filenames, SVG/HTML stored XSS, and ZipSlip extraction.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-ASVS-V5, OWASP-ASVS-V13, OWASP-API3:2023, OWASP-API8:2023, CWE-79, CWE-22, CWE-1336

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- productionBrowserSourceMaps: false in next.config.js / vite.config.ts
- Explicit session & role verification inside every Next.js Server Action ('use server') and getServerSideProps
- Strict event.origin allowlist check in window.addEventListener('message', ...) before processing payload
- Parameterized queries and context-aware auto-escaping without dangerouslySetInnerHTML or raw template compilation

### Vulnerable Patterns
- productionBrowserSourceMaps: true or exposed *.js.map files in public S3/CDN buckets
- NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*, or REACT_APP_* variables containing internal API keys, client secrets, or static HMAC keys
- Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflecting arbitrary Origin headers with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
- Uncanonicalized path.join(uploadDir, req.file.originalname) or dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: userContent }}

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of build/bundler config (next.config.js, vite.config.ts, angular.json) or server route/action handler
- ev_... excerpt of CORS middleware configuration or postMessage event handler showing origin validation logic

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are source maps (*.js.map) stripped in the CI/CD production deployment stage or blocked at the CDN/Cloudflare edge?
- Does an upstream reverse proxy override or sanitize Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers before responses reach the browser?

# Mobile Super-Apps & Companion Apps (Android/Kotlin/Smali, iOS/Swift, Flutter, BLE) (`mobile-android-ios-flutter`)

> **Group:** I. Web, Mobile & API Core
> **Product Archetypes:** Mobile_Client_Android_iOS, Connected_Vehicle_Companion_App
> **Trigger Signals:** android, ios, kotlin, swift, flutter, dart, react-native, retrofit, okhttp, smali, apk, deeplink, bluetooth, ble, firebase

## [ BLOCK: mobile-exported-components-and-deeplinks ]
### Exported Activities/Services/Receivers, DeepLinks & WebView Bridges
- Audit `AndroidManifest.xml` (`android:exported="true"`, intent filters, custom URL schemes) and iOS `Info.plist` Universal Links.
- Trace untrusted DeepLink parameters flowing into `WebView.loadUrl()`, `addJavascriptInterface`, or internal authenticated API calls.
- Verify whether tokens or session cookies are automatically attached when a WebView loads an attacker-controlled URL.

## [ BLOCK: dynamic-host-routing-and-client-signing ]
### Retrofit/OkHttp Interceptors, Firebase Remote Config & Static Signing
- Enumerate ALL Retrofit/OkHttp service modules (do not stop at the primary client; check secondary modules like Auth0, Guest, EV, OwnerManual).
- Inspect `DynamicHostInterceptor` / Firebase Remote Config routing that switches endpoints per region or environment.
- Refute client-side HMAC/request-signing theater (`X-HASH`, static secrets in native `.so` or Dart/Kotlin constants) — treat client-known secrets as public.

## [ BLOCK: ble-phone-as-a-key-and-device-ota ]
### BLE Phone-as-a-Key (PAAK) & Mobile-Relayed Firmware Updates
- When the mobile app acts as a BLE key (e.g., eScooter/Vehicle PAAK) or relays firmware (`Cloud -> Phone -> BLE -> Vehicle`), trace pairing, nonce/anti-replay, and key revocation on lending/transfer.
- Verify whether the mobile app can flash downgraded or modified firmware packages onto the vehicle/device over BLE.

## [ BLOCK: masvs-local-storage-keystore-and-cert-pinning ]
### MASVS Local Storage, Android Keystore / iOS Keychain & Certificate Pinning
- Audit local persistence (`SharedPreferences`, `MMKV`, `SQLite`, `Realm`, `UserDefaults`, `FlutterSecureStorage`, external storage) for plaintext tokens, PII, VINs, or BLE keys.
- Verify hardware-backed `AndroidKeyStore` / iOS Keychain (`kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`) usage with biometric/user-presence binding where required.
- Inspect `network_security_config.xml`, `OkHttpCertificatePinner`, `TrustManager`, and Flutter `SecurityContext` for disabled TLS verification (`checkServerTrusted` no-op, `badCertificateCallback => true`) or expired/missing certificate pins.

### Standard Mappings
- MASVS-STORAGE-1, MASVS-STORAGE-2, MASVS-CRYPTO-1, MASVS-NETWORK-1, MASVS-NETWORK-2, MASVS-PLATFORM-1, ISO-SAE-21434

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- EncryptedSharedPreferences / iOS Keychain with hardware-backed KeyStore and kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly
- OkHttp CertificatePinner with valid SHA-256 public key pins and no debug TrustManager overrides in release builds
- android:exported="false" on internal Activities/Services/BroadcastReceivers and strict host/scheme validation on DeepLinks
- Ephemeral ECDH + monotonic nonce/counter validation on BLE Phone-as-a-Key (PAAK) GATT command frames

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Plaintext JWT/refresh tokens or vehicle BLE keys written to MODE_WORLD_READABLE SharedPreferences, SQLite, or logcat
- Custom X509TrustManager with empty checkServerTrusted() or HostnameVerifier returning true
- Exported WebView Activity loading untrusted Intent extras via webView.loadUrl() with JavaScript and universal file access enabled
- Hardcoded HMAC signing secrets or OAuth client secrets embedded in Kotlin/Swift constants, Dart snapshots, or JNI .so binaries

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of AndroidManifest.xml / Info.plist showing exported components and intent-filter / Universal Link definitions
- ev_... excerpt of network client initialization (OkHttp/Retrofit/Dio) and token storage implementation

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is certificate pinning enforced via an external SDK or mobile app shielding wrapper applied post-compilation?
- Are BLE digital keys revoked immediately on the vehicle BCM/T-Box when ownership or lending status changes in the cloud?

# REST, GraphQL, gRPC/Protobuf & WebSocket API Surfaces (`api-rest-graphql-grpc-websocket`)

> **Group:** I. Web, Mobile & API Core
> **Product Archetypes:** API_Microservice_Gateway, Realtime_WebSocket_Service
> **Trigger Signals:** openapi, swagger, rest, graphql, grpc, protobuf, proto, websocket, ws, wss, ssrf, webhook, fileupload, multipart

## [ BLOCK: openapi-shadow-routes-and-debug-sinks ]
### Undocumented Shadow Routes, Staging Backdoors & Schema Exposure
- Compare code-level route registrations against published OpenAPI/Swagger specs to uncover shadow endpoints.
- Hunt for non-prod/test/debug handlers (`/fake/otp/*`, `/test/user-vehicle/*`, `/api/sample/*`, `/actuator/*`, Django `DEBUG=True` URL dumps) compiled into shared builds.

## [ BLOCK: ssrf-webhooks-and-url-fetchers ]
### Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), Webhooks & Media/Avatar Fetchers
- Trace all user-supplied URLs (webhooks, avatar/document imports, OIDC discovery, PDF/headless-browser rendering) to outbound HTTP clients.
- Check if DNS resolution, HTTP redirects (301/302), or IPv6 mapped addresses bypass RFC1918 (`10.x.x.x`) and cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`) filters.

## [ BLOCK: websocket-and-grpc-stream-auth ]
### WebSocket Upgrade Handshake, Message-Level Authz & gRPC Interceptors
- Verify whether WebSocket (`ws://`/`wss://`) servers validate `Origin`, authenticate the HTTP `101 Switching Protocols` upgrade, AND enforce per-message/per-topic authorization.
- Check gRPC unary and streaming interceptors for unauthenticated reflection or missing metadata token checks.

## [ BLOCK: api3-bopla-mass-assignment-and-data-exposure ]
### OWASP API3:2023 BOPLA — Mass Assignment & Excessive Data Exposure
- Check whether request DTOs/models bind directly to ORM entities (`Object.assign`, `Model.create(req.body)`, `BeanUtils.copyProperties`, Pydantic/Jackson/Ginauto-binding) allowing privilege/role/balance/status tampering.
- Check whether response serializers return raw database entities leaking sensitive fields (`passwordHash`, `otpCode`, internal tenant metadata, PII).

## [ BLOCK: api4-rate-limiting-pagination-and-resource-dos ]
### OWASP API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption, Pagination & Batch DoS
- Verify upper bounds on pagination parameters (`limit`, `pageSize`, `first`), GraphQL query depth/complexity, batch array sizes, and synchronous report/export endpoints.
- Check for missing per-user/per-IP rate limiting on expensive compute, SMS/email dispatch, or third-party billing calls.

## [ BLOCK: asvs-v5-file-upload-path-traversal-zipslip-and-injection ]
### ASVS V5 File Upload, Path Traversal, ZipSlip & General Injection (SQLi/Cmd/NoSQLi/SSTI)
- Trace multipart file uploads and archive extractors (`zipfile`, `tarfile`, `ZipInputStream`) for `../` Path Traversal / ZipSlip, unrestricted file extensions, and SSRF via SVG/XML (XXE).
- Hunt for raw string interpolation in SQL queries, NoSQL operators (`$where`, `$gt`, `$ne`), OS command execution (`subprocess`, `exec`, `Runtime.exec`), and template engines.

## [ BLOCK: asvs-v16-logging-error-handling-and-audit-integrity ]
### ASVS V16 Security Logging, Error Handling & Audit Trail Tampering
- Check global exception handlers for stack trace, SQL query, or internal environment leakage in error responses.
- Verify that security-critical mutations emit immutable audit logs resistant to log injection (CRLF/JSON spoofing) and silent exception swallowing.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API3:2023, OWASP-API4:2023, OWASP-API7:2023, OWASP-API8:2023, OWASP-API9:2023, ASVS-V5, ASVS-V13, ASVS-V16

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Explicit allowlisted Request/Response DTOs with strict field-level validation and no direct ORM entity binding
- Enforced maximum pageSize cap (e.g., Math.min(limit, 100)) and rate-limiting middleware on public/expensive routes
- Parameterized SQL queries, canonicalized path verification (Path.resolve().startsWith(baseDir)), and ZipEntry path checks
- Structured JSON audit logging with sanitized fields and generic client error messages hiding internal stack traces

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Direct binding of req.body / request JSON into ORM update/save calls allowing role, balance, or tenant_id mass assignment
- Unbounded pagination (LIMIT $limit without cap), unthrottled batch arrays, or deeply nested GraphQL queries
- Archive extraction or file write using unvalidated entry.getName() / filename allowing ../ ZipSlip or path traversal
- String-concatenated SQL/NoSQL/shell commands or outbound HTTP fetchers accepting unvalidated user URLs (SSRF)

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of controller/router endpoint signature, request DTO/schema definition, and response serializer
- ev_... excerpt of downstream service/DAO query, file handler, or outbound HTTP client call

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are pagination limits, payload size caps, or rate limits enforced at an upstream API Gateway (Kong/KrakenD) rather than in application code?
- Are uploaded files scanned and rewritten by an isolated object-storage worker before being served to users?

# Authorization, BOLA/IDOR, BFLA & Multi-Tenant / Partner Isolation (`authz-bola-bfla-multitenant`)

> **Group:** I. Web, Mobile & API Core
> **Product Archetypes:** API_Microservice_Gateway, B2B_Partner_Portal, Multi_Tenant_SaaS
> **Trigger Signals:** authz, bola, idor, bfla, rbac, abac, preauthorize, permission, ownership, tenant, vincode, billid, orderid, partnerid

## [ BLOCK: object-ownership-bola-idor ]
### Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) on Resource Identifiers
- For every endpoint accepting an object identifier (`vinCode`, `billId`, `orderId`, `tokenNumber`, `target` Cognito ID, `partnerId`), verify a deterministic join/check binding the authenticated subject (`sub`/`userId`) to that object.
- Check both read paths (e.g., `/parked-images`, `/bills/{id}`) and state-changing paths (`DELETE /cards/{token}`, `POST /transfer-ownership`, `POST /attach-policy`).

## [ BLOCK: function-level-bfla-and-filter-bypass ]
### Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA) & Security Filter Chain Bypass
- Compare controller-level and method-level guards across sibling routes (e.g., `/user/**`, `/admin/**`, `/internal/**`).
- Check for path matching discrepancies between API Gateway (Kong/KrakenD/ALB) and backend framework (Spring Security Ant/PathPattern matcher, trailing slash, matrix params `;`).

## [ BLOCK: multi-role-lending-and-delegation ]
### Temporary Delegation, Vehicle Lending/Valet Mode & Ownership Transfer
- Trace lifecycle revocation: when a vehicle/asset is transferred or a secondary driver/valet permission expires, are active JWTs, refresh tokens, AWS IoT policies, and BLE digital keys immediately revoked?

## [ BLOCK: bopla-field-level-authz-and-tenant-context-spoofing ]
### Object Property Level Authz (BOPLA) & Cross-Tenant Context Spoofing
- Verify whether callers can overwrite `tenantId`, `partnerId`, `ownerId`, `vinCode`, or `role` in PUT/PATCH/POST bodies or query parameters to pivot across tenants.
- Check whether list/search/export endpoints enforce tenant and ownership predicates inside the database WHERE clause rather than filtering only in UI or post-query code.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API1:2023, OWASP-API3:2023, OWASP-API5:2023, ASVS-V4, CWE-639, CWE-285, CWE-862

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Database query scopes resource lookup by both object ID and authenticated subject/tenant from verified JWT security context (WHERE id = :id AND owner_id = :sub)
- Method-level and route-level RBAC/ABAC guards (@PreAuthorize, Depends(require_role), policy enforcer) verified on all sibling and admin endpoints
- Immediate revocation of delegated/secondary driver permissions and cached sessions upon asset ownership transfer

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Repository lookup by primary key alone (findById(id)) without verifying resource.ownerId == currentUser.id
- Trusting client-supplied userId, tenantId, partnerId, or vinCode from request body/header/query instead of the authenticated token subject
- Admin or internal state-changing endpoints missing role guards or relying on easily bypassed URL path prefix matching

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of the route handler and security guard/middleware wiring
- ev_... excerpt of the service/repository method showing whether authenticated subject/tenant ownership is enforced on the target object ID

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is row-level security (RLS) or a global ORM tenant filter automatically injected by a shared database library not visible in this repository?
- Does an external policy engine (OPA / IAM authorizer) validate resource ownership before forwarding the request?

# State Machines, Race Conditions (TOCTOU), Payments, Billing & E-Commerce (`state-race-financial-commerce`)

> **Group:** I. Web, Mobile & API Core
> **Product Archetypes:** Payment_Billing_Service, Ecommerce_Portal, Subscription_OTA_Commerce
> **Trigger Signals:** payment, billing, invoice, order, cart, checkout, voucher, coupon, wallet, refund, deposit, subscription, idempotency, lock, transaction

## [ BLOCK: toctou-race-and-idempotency ]
### Concurrent State Mutation (TOCTOU), Double-Spend & Missing Idempotency
- Inspect balance/voucher redemptions, refund triggers, OTP verifications, and ownership transfers for read-modify-write without `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, atomic conditional update, or distributed lock.
- Verify whether idempotency keys are scoped to `(userId, endpoint, payload_hash)` and cannot be replayed across different parameters.

## [ BLOCK: payment-webhook-and-ota-entitlement ]
### Payment Callback Forgery, Price/Currency Tampering & Paid OTA Entitlement
- Verify cryptographic signature validation and state transition ordering on payment gateway webhooks.
- In paid FOTA/SOTA or e-commerce flows, check whether an attacker can trigger fulfillment/installation before payment settlement completes.

## [ BLOCK: asvs-v7-otp-rate-limit-and-voucher-replay ]
### OTP/PIN Brute-Force, Coupon/Voucher Replay & Partial Refund Loops
- Verify strict attempt counters, exponential backoff, and single-use atomic invalidation on OTP, PIN, gift card, and promo code redemption endpoints.
- Check whether partial refunds, split payments, or negative quantity/amount values cause arithmetic underflow or double-crediting.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API4:2023, OWASP-API6:2023, ASVS-V4, ASVS-V7, ASVS-V11, CWE-362, CWE-841

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Pessimistic row locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) or single atomic conditional UPDATE (WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND balance >= :amount)
- Idempotency key bound to (user_id, endpoint, request_payload_hash) stored atomically with the state transition
- Cryptographic HMAC/RSA signature verification and strict state-machine transition guards on payment gateway webhooks

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Read-modify-write balance/voucher check in application memory followed by a separate non-locking save/update
- Payment webhook handler updating order status to PAID without verifying gateway signature or checking prior terminal state
- Missing validation against negative quantities, negative transfer amounts, or currency mismatch between order creation and settlement

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of the transaction/service method performing state check and balance/order mutation
- ev_... excerpt of the database locking, idempotency middleware, or webhook signature verification logic

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Does a distributed lock (Redis Redlock) or database unique constraint / serializable isolation level prevent concurrent duplicate execution?
- Is payment webhook authenticity verified by an upstream payment gateway adapter before reaching this service?

iam-auth0-cognito-azuread-fido2.title: Identity Fabric: Auth0, AWS Cognito, Azure AD, FIDO2/WebAuthn & Internal JWT
safe_patterns: Strict JWT verification pinning allowed asymmetric algorithms (RS256/ES256), expected issuer (iss), audience (aud), and expiration (exp)
Single-use cryptographically random password-reset / OTP tokens with strict per-account attempt lockout and TTL <= 10 minutes
Refresh token rotation with reuse detection and immediate server-side session revocation on password/privilege change
vulnerable_patterns: JWT decoding without signature verification (jwt.decode(..., options={'verify_signature': False}), parseClaimsJwt) or accepting alg: none
Cognito Identity Pool allowing unauthenticated identities with over-privileged IAM/IoT policy attachment
OTP or password-reset verification lacking per-target attempt counters, allowing brute-force or cross-user token replay
required_evidence: ev_... excerpt of JWT/OIDC verifier configuration showing issuer, audience, and signature algorithm checks
ev_... excerpt of session/refresh-token lifecycle, OTP verification, or STS/IoT policy vending handler
questions_when_unclear: Is brute-force lockout or token revocation enforced directly within the upstream IdP (Auth0 / Cognito / Azure AD) tenant configuration?
What IAM permissions are attached to the Cognito Unauthenticated Role in the production AWS account?

# Identity Fabric: Auth0, AWS Cognito, Azure AD, FIDO2/WebAuthn & Internal JWT (`iam-auth0-cognito-azuread-fido2`)

> **Group:** II. Identity, Gateways & Multi-Cloud / On-Prem
> **Product Archetypes:** Identity_SSO_Provider, API_Microservice_Gateway
> **Trigger Signals:** auth0, cognito, azuread, entra, oidc, oauth, saml, fido2, webauthn, jwt, jwks, nimbus, sts, refresh_token

## [ BLOCK: jwt-issuer-audience-and-token-exchange ]
### Multi-Tenant JWT Validation, Audience Isolation & Refresh Token Exchange
- Verify strict validation of `iss`, `aud`, `alg` (no `none` or RS256->HS256 confusion), and `exp`.
- Audit token-exchange and refresh endpoints (e.g., `/exchange-refresh-token`) for missing client authentication, scope escalation, or cross-region token acceptance.

## [ BLOCK: cognito-identity-pools-and-sts-vending ]
### AWS Cognito Unauthenticated Pools, STS Vending & Policy Attachment
- Check Cognito Identity Pools for `AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities` and inspect the IAM/IoT permissions bound to the Unauth Role.
- Audit backend endpoints that vend AWS STS credentials (`/client/credentials`) or attach policies (`/attach-policy`) to ensure caller identity and resource ownership are verified.

## [ BLOCK: fido2-webauthn-and-qr-sso ]
### FIDO2/WebAuthn Attestation/Assertion & Cross-Device QR/SSE Login
- In WebAuthn flows (`/attestation/result`, `/assertion/result`, `/recovery/key`), verify server-side challenge single-use binding, `rpId` verification, and signCount checks.
- In QR-code / SSE login flows (`/qr/:type/:sseEncryptKey/:signature/:nonce`), check for session fixation or cross-user QR approval hijacking.

## [ BLOCK: asvs-v7-session-revocation-password-reset-and-otp-bruteforce ]
### ASVS V7 Session/Token Revocation, Password Reset Poisoning & OTP Brute-Force
- Verify server-side revocation of active JWTs/refresh tokens upon logout, password change, role downgrade, or account lock (`jti` denylist / token version check).
- Audit password reset and account recovery flows for Host-header poisoning, predictable reset tokens, token reuse, and missing OTP brute-force lockout (e.g., 4-6 digit OTP without attempt cap).

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API2:2023, ASVS-V2, ASVS-V3, ASVS-V7, CWE-287, CWE-307, CWE-613, CWE-640

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Strict JWT verification pinning allowed asymmetric algorithms (RS256/ES256), expected issuer (iss), audience (aud), and expiration (exp)
- Single-use cryptographically random password-reset / OTP tokens with strict per-account attempt lockout and TTL <= 10 minutes
- Refresh token rotation with reuse detection and immediate server-side session revocation on password/privilege change

### Vulnerable Patterns
- JWT decoding without signature verification (jwt.decode(..., options={'verify_signature': False}), parseClaimsJwt) or accepting alg: none
- Cognito Identity Pool allowing unauthenticated identities with over-privileged IAM/IoT policy attachment
- OTP or password-reset verification lacking per-target attempt counters, allowing brute-force or cross-user token replay

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of JWT/OIDC verifier configuration showing issuer, audience, and signature algorithm checks
- ev_... excerpt of session/refresh-token lifecycle, OTP verification, or STS/IoT policy vending handler

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is brute-force lockout or token revocation enforced directly within the upstream IdP (Auth0 / Cognito / Azure AD) tenant configuration?
- What IAM permissions are attached to the Cognito Unauthenticated Role in the production AWS account?

## [ BLOCK: asymmetric-edge-and-direct-origin-bypass ]

- Check whether regional or staging gateways (e.g., Bare AWS ALBs, GCP direct IPs, DR endpoints) expose the same backend Kong/KrakenD services without Cloudflare WAF protection.
- Verify whether management interfaces (Kong Admin `:8001/:8444`, KrakenD debug/config endpoints, Spring Actuator) are reachable on direct origins.

## [ BLOCK: gateway-header-spoofing-and-contract-shims ]
### Static Gateway Headers (x-device-platform) & Trusted Header Spoofing
- Refute security controls that rely solely on static client headers (`x-device-platform: android`, `x-service-name`).
- Check whether backend services trust `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Authenticated-Userid`, or `X-Consumer-*` headers when requests bypass the gateway or arrive via an untrusted ingress.

## [ BLOCK: api4-gateway-rate-limiting-and-body-size-enforcement ]
### Gateway Rate-Limiting, Payload Size Caps & Upstream Timeout Hardening
- Verify whether Kong/KrakenD/Nginx/ALB configurations enforce rate-limiting plugins, `client_max_body_size`, and header sanitization before forwarding to microservices.
- Check whether internal/admin routes (`/actuator`, `/metrics`, `/swagger`, `/internal/*`) are explicitly blocked on public ingress rules.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API4:2023, OWASP-API8:2023, ASVS-V13, ASVS-V14, CWE-290, CWE-770

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Origin ALB/Ingress restricted to Cloudflare IP ranges + authenticated Origin Pull mTLS certificates
- Gateway strips untrusted client-supplied X-Authenticated-Userid, X-Consumer-*, and X-Forwarded-For headers before injecting verified identity claims
- Explicit deny rules blocking /internal/*, /actuator/*, and Kong Admin (:8001/:8444) on external listeners

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Direct internet-facing Bare ALB or public IP exposing backend services without WAF or mTLS origin authentication
- Backend trusting X-Forwarded-For, X-Device-Platform, or X-User-Id headers directly from unverified ingress paths
- KrakenD/Kong route definitions exposing debug endpoints or forwarding all headers ("input_headers": ["*"]) without stripping identity headers

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of gateway config (krakend.json, kong.yml, nginx.conf, Ingress/ALB Terraform/Helm) showing route and header rules
- ev_... excerpt of backend middleware reading identity or client IP headers

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Do AWS Security Groups or network ACLs restrict the origin ALB to Cloudflare IP CIDRs only?
- Does the API Gateway overwrite or strip client-supplied identity headers before forwarding requests upstream?

- Inspect CNAME records pointing to unprovisioned Azure App Services (`*.azurewebsites.net`), S3/GCS buckets, or dangling CloudFront distributions.
- Verify TLS certificate validity and CA issuance across multi-cloud endpoints.

## [ BLOCK: cloud-storage-pre-signed-urls-and-iam ]
### S3/GCS/Azure Blob ACLs, Pre-Signed URL Scope & Cross-Account IAM
- Check whether staging/prod buckets (`gcs`, `s3`) allow public listing or leak sourcemaps, backups, or vehicle camera images.
- Verify whether shared AWS accounts across dev/staging regions allow cross-environment privilege escalation via overly broad IAM/KMS policies.

## [ BLOCK: asvs-v5-storage-upload-validation-and-path-prefix-isolation ]
### Pre-Signed Upload Key Prefix Traversal & Content-Type Enforcement
- Check whether S3/GCS/Azure Blob pre-signed upload URL generators allow caller-controlled object keys (`../../other-tenant/file` or overwriting static web assets).
- Verify whether pre-signed PUT/POST policies constrain `Content-Type`, maximum file size (`content-length-range`), and tenant key prefixes.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API8:2023, ASVS-V5, ASVS-V14, CWE-22, CWE-284, CWE-732

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Server-generated UUID object keys under a strict tenant prefix (${tenantId}/${uuid}) with Content-Type and size conditions on pre-signed URLs
- S3 PublicAccessBlock enabled and IAM policies scoped to least-privilege resource ARNs without wildcard s3:* or sts:AssumeRole *
- Automated DNS lifecycle cleanup removing CNAME records before deprovisioning cloud apps or buckets

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Generating pre-signed S3/GCS PUT/GET URLs directly from user-supplied file paths or bucket names without ownership/prefix validation
- Publicly listable or readable S3/GCS/Azure Blob buckets containing customer KYC docs, vehicle camera images, or build sourcemaps
- IAM roles with Action: '*' and Resource: '*' shared across dev, staging, and production workloads

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of S3/GCS/Blob client code generating pre-signed URLs or performing object reads/writes
- ev_... excerpt of IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation/Helm) defining bucket ACLs and IAM role policies

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is S3 Block Public Access enabled at the AWS Account level and enforced via AWS Organizations SCP?
- Are bucket policies restricting object access to specific VPC Endpoints?

### Azure DevOps (ADO) & GitHub Actions Expression Injection & Token Permissions
- Check `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `azure-pipelines.yml` for dangerous triggers (`pull_request_target`), unpinned third-party actions/tasks (`@v*` instead of commit SHA), and missing `permissions:` blocks.
- Trace untrusted PR branch names, commit messages, or issue titles interpolated into `run:` / `script:` blocks.

## [ BLOCK: argocd-gitops-and-binary-provenance ]
### ArgoCD GitOps Control Plane & Prebuilt Binary / Dependency Provenance
- Verify authentication, RBAC, and webhook secret validation on ArgoCD (`argocd.ccar-internal`) and container registries.
- Flag unverified prebuilt native binaries (`.so`, `.dll`, `.onnx`) committed directly into repositories or downloaded in `setup.sh` without SHA-256 checksum pinning.

## [ BLOCK: pipeline-secret-masking-and-audit-tampering ]
### Pipeline Secret Leakage, Artifact Tampering & Audit Log Integrity
- Check build scripts for `env`, `printenv`, `set -x`, or verbose debug flags that dump CI/CD secrets into build logs.
- Verify whether build artifacts and container images are cryptographically signed (Cosign/SLSA) and verified before ArgoCD deployment.

### Standard Mappings
- SLSA-v1.0, NIST-SSDF, ASVS-V14, ASVS-V16, CWE-78, CWE-494, CWE-829

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- GitHub Actions / ADO tasks pinned to full 40-char commit SHAs with minimal read-only GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
- Untrusted PR metadata (github.head_ref, pr.title) passed via environment variables rather than inline ${{ ... }} shell interpolation
- SHA-256 checksum and Cosign signature verification on all downloaded binaries, models, and container images

### Vulnerable Patterns
- pull_request_target workflow checking out untrusted PR head code and executing package scripts with write tokens/secrets
- Direct interpolation of ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} or $(System.PullRequest.SourceBranch) inside run:/script: shell blocks
- curl | bash or unpinned binary/model downloads in Dockerfiles and setup scripts without cryptographic hash verification

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of .github/workflows/*.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, Jenkinsfile, or Dockerfile
- ev_... excerpt of ArgoCD Application manifest or deployment script showing image/binary verification

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are branch protection rules and mandatory code-owner reviews enforced on the repository before CI pipelines execute?
- Does an enterprise artifact proxy (Nexus/Artifactory) verify package signatures upstream?

- Verify whether WebSocket (`ws://`/`wss://`) servers validate `Origin`, authenticate the HTTP `101 Switching Protocols` upgrade, AND enforce per-message/per-topic authorization.

- Verify upper bounds on pagination parameters (`limit`, `pageSize`, `first`), GraphQL query depth/complexity, batch array sizes, and synchronous report/export endpoints.
- Check for missing per-user/per-IP rate limiting on expensive compute, SMS/email dispatch, or third-party billing calls.

## [ BLOCK: unauthenticated-robot-and-ipc-command-bridges ]
### Unauthenticated HTTP/ZeroMQ/MQTT-to-Robot Actuation Bridges & Bounds Checks
- Hunt for unauthenticated network bridges (e.g., HTTP `/api/sample/call-command/` forwarding directly to EMQX `:8883`, or ZeroMQ `tcp://*:5555` `PredictRequest` servers without CURVE auth).
- Verify protobuf/message field-level bounds validation (image dimensions, view counts, joint velocity/torque limits) beyond simple total byte-size caps.

## [ BLOCK: ot-scada-bess-and-ai-in-control-loop ]
### OT SCADA/BESS (IEC 62443), 3-Party Trust Boundaries & AI-in-the-Control-Loop
- When AI forecasting models feed into OT/SCADA control loops (e.g., BESS 50MW/100MWh charge/discharge scheduling, BF-BOF furnace gas valves, or ATO rail signaling), verify whether a deterministic, hardware/PLC-enforced safety interlock independently clamps out-of-range commands regardless of AI output.
- Map 3-party trust boundaries (`Asset Owner <-> Grid/Plant Operator <-> Control Software Vendor`) and flag any remote maintenance/telemetry channel lacking dual-path isolation or safety-owner sign-off.

## [ BLOCK: ot-command-injection-bounds-and-safety-audit ]
### C++/IPC Memory Safety, Command Rate-Limiting & Immutable Safety Audit Logs
- In C++/ROS2/ZeroMQ services, audit deserialization buffers, image/tensor dimensions, and array indices for integer overflow and out-of-bounds memory access.
- Verify message rate-limiting (API4) on ZeroMQ/MQTT/Modbus command buses and tamper-evident safety audit logging (ASVS V16) whenever an emergency stop, setpoint override, or BMS/PLC command is issued.

### Standard Mappings
- IEC-62443-3-3, IEC-62443-4-2, ISO-10218, ISO-26262, NIST-AI-RMF, OWASP-API4:2023, ASVS-V5, ASVS-V16

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- ZeroMQ CURVE / ROS2 SROS2 DDS security / mTLS authentication on all IPC and network actuation sockets
- Deterministic hardware/PLC safety interlock and kinematic/power setpoint clamping independent of AI/cloud control outputs
- Strict bounds checking on protobuf/ZeroMQ frame sizes, tensor dimensions, and joint velocity/torque/MW setpoints before execution

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Unauthenticated ZeroMQ (tcp://*:5555), ROS2 DDS, Modbus TCP, or HTTP-to-MQTT bridge forwarding raw actuation commands to robots/BESS
- AI/LLM/forecasting output wired directly into PLC/BMS/robot actuators without an independent deterministic bounds filter
- Unchecked integer arithmetic on frame dimensions or payload lengths before heap allocation or memcpy in C/C++ handlers

- ev_... excerpt of C++/Python/Go IPC listener (ZeroMQ/ROS2/MQTT/Modbus) showing authentication and message parsing
- ev_... excerpt of actuation dispatch logic showing bounds checks or safety interlock validation

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Is the robot/BESS control subnet physically air-gapped or segmented via unidirectional data diodes / OT firewalls (IEC 62443 Zone & Conduit)?
- Does an independent safety PLC or hardware BMS hard-clamp power, thermal, and torque limits regardless of software commands?
